entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-vmhf-c436-hxj4: JupyterLab: Stored XSS in extension manager through package metadata unsanitized URI protocol
entry.content:
JupyterLab: Stored XSS in extension manager through package metadata unsanitized URI protocol

Aliases: BIT-jupyterlab-2026-67338, CVE-2026-67338

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N

Affected:

  • jupyterlab — fixed in 4.5.9

A malicious PyPI package can place a `javascript:` URL in its `[project.urls]` metadata. JupyterLab's Extension Manager renders this as the extension's home-page link without validating the protocol, so a user who clicks the extension name executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the JupyterLab origin. ### Details One of the PyPI package's URL (jupyterlab/extensions/pypi.py) is copied straight into the `homepage_url` rendered by the frontend in packages/extensionmanager/src/widget.tsx#L77-L88. ```python best_guess_home_url = ( homepage_url # home_page / [project.urls] Homepage or data.get("project_url") or data.get("package_url") or documentation_url # docs_url / [project.urls] Documentation or source_url # [project.urls] Source Code or …

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-9w56-46f6-3qhx: asteval Sandbox Escape: arbitrary native memory read/write via numpy ctypes in default asteval Interpreter
entry.content:
asteval Sandbox Escape: arbitrary native memory read/write via numpy ctypes in default asteval Interpreter

Aliases: CVE-2026-102734

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • asteval — fixed in 1.0.9

### Summary With its default configuration (numpy enabled, `import` disabled), asteval's `Interpreter` lets an attacker-controlled expression obtain a raw **arbitrary process-memory read and write** primitive, without using `import`, any `__dunder__` attribute, or `eval`/`exec`/`getattr`. Arbitrary in-process read/write is equivalent to arbitrary code execution and is a complete escape of the sandbox whose entire purpose is "untrusted string in, no arbitrary execution out." Any application that feeds untrusted input to asteval with numpy installed (the default) is affected. ### Details asteval's attribute filter (`asteval/astutils.py: safe_getattr`) blocks every `__dunder__` name and blocks objects whose attribute value is *identity-equal* to one of the modules in `UNSAFE_MODULES = {io, o…

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17866: Malicious code in pyyi (PyPI)
entry.content:
Malicious code in pyyi (PyPI)

Affected:

  • pyyi

The verified PyPI wheel declares a console command named python2 (pyyi.cli:main). For commands other than the local REPL, help, version, unlock, or uninstall paths, it obtains configuration and calls run_payload(). Registration sends the hostname and OS to a configured space-z.ai server and stores the returned apiKey in ~/.python2/config.json. The REPL presents a normal Python banner but silently sends eligible single-token inputs to /api/cli/unlock as the password field, subject to filtering and attempt limits. run_payload() fetches code from /api/cli/payload, base64-decodes and gzip-decompresses it, then executes it in memory using exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g) at pyyi/cli.py:640 and calls its main function. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-hj66-6f7g-4r5v: Oauthlib : Unsafe JSONP callback injection in RevocationEndpoint allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation
entry.content:
Oauthlib : Unsafe JSONP callback injection in RevocationEndpoint allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation

Aliases: CVE-2026-49264, PYSEC-2026-4113

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • oauthlib — fixed in 4.0.0

### Summary When `enable_jsonp=True`, oauthlib's `RevocationEndpoint` reflects the user-supplied `callback` parameter directly into JavaScript response bodies on both success and error paths without validating that it is a legal JSONP callback name. This allows arbitrary JavaScript response generation instead of a restricted function call, making the documented JSONP revocation feature unsafe for browser-based JSONP consumption when attackers can influence `callback`. ### Details The issue is in `oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/endpoints/revocation.py`. When `enable_jsonp=True` is passed to the `RevocationEndpoint` constructor, two code paths wrap the response body using the user-supplied `request.callback` parameter: ```python # Error response path (line 72-73): if self.enable_jsonp and requ…

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-2946: PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands
entry.content:
PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands

Aliases: CVE-2026-56074, GHSA-ffp3-3562-8cv3

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • praisonaiagents — fixed in 4.5.128

## Summary The approval system in PraisonAI Agents caches tool approval decisions by tool name only, not by invocation arguments. Once a user approves `execute_command` for any command (e.g., `ls -la`), all subsequent `execute_command` calls in that execution context bypass the approval prompt entirely. Combined with `os.environ.copy()` passing all process environment variables to subprocesses, this allows an LLM agent (potentially via prompt injection) to silently exfiltrate API keys and credentials without further user consent. ## Details The `require_approval` decorator in `src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/approval/__init__.py:176-178` checks approval status by tool name only: ```python @wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): if is_already_approved(tool_name): # line 17…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-q238-5cxm-5c9h: Django GeoDjango vulnerable to denial of service through deeply nested geometry collections
entry.content:
Django GeoDjango vulnerable to denial of service through deeply nested geometry collections

Aliases: BIT-django-2026-15830, CVE-2026-15830, PYSEC-2026-3717

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • django — fixed in 5.2.17
  • django — fixed in 6.0.8
  • django — fixed in 6.1.1

An issue was discovered in Django 5.2 before 5.2.17 and 6.0 before 6.0.8. GeoDjango's `django.contrib.gis.geos.GEOSGeometry` is subject to a potential denial-of-service when parsing deeply nested `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` objects supplied as well-known text (WKT), well-known binary (WKB), or hex-encoded WKB, which triggers unbounded recursion and a segmentation fault in the underlying GEOS library. Spatial field lookups and the `django.contrib.gis.forms.GeometryField` form field are also affected. Earlier, unsupported Django series (such as 5.1.x, 5.0.x, and 4.2.x) were not evaluated and may also be affected. Django would like to thank Andrew MacPherson and kimchunbok_ for reporting this issue.

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17807: Malicious code in py2ops (PyPI)
entry.content:
Malicious code in py2ops (PyPI)

Affected:

  • py2ops

The package installs a console command named python2 (pyops.cli:main), so it runs when someone types python2. On first run _register() in cli.py POSTs the hostname and OS to a space-z.ai server and keeps the returned apiKey in ~/.python2/config.json. Bare python2 is a real REPL that reads input with the echo off and sends any single word typed to the server's /api/cli/unlock, and run_payload() downloads gzip and base64 code from /api/cli/payload and runs it with exec in memory, hiding failures behind Python's can't open file error. Comments in the file call this the cover. I did not see what the served code does. I read 2.2 and did not run it.

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17712: Malicious code in ig-gox (PyPI)
entry.content:
Malicious code in ig-gox (PyPI)

Affected:

  • ig-gox

Importing ig_gox runs ig_gox/__init__.py, which decodes a blob (base64, XOR, zlib) after a few anti-debugging checks and execs it as __main__. The decoded loader only goes on if it looks like a physical Android device running Termux (it turns away x86, emulators and VMs), installs requests and cryptography if they are missing, downloads encrypted code from https://goxtools.shop/api/admin/storage.php, decrypts it with AES-256-CBC and runs it in memory. The README only calls it a runtime engine for Termux. I decoded the loader statically and did not see what the downloaded code does. I read 1.0.0 and did not run it. --- _-= Per source details.
